judgements.reason: You are not alone; the stuckness is inward and needs a change of soul.
General theory of boredom; doesn't meet the comparison or self-doubt.
Questions whether others' visible happiness is real; eases the comparison.
Boredom is ancient, your capacities unmeasured; don't despair of what's left.
Follow your own genius and life shows fresh prospects; a way forward.
About youth versus age and illusions of happiness; mostly beside the point.
Others' amusements hide despair; bleak and offers little to someone stuck.
Mirrors 'everyone else is happy, I alone am listless' without offering more.
Generic line on enthusiasm; doesn't speak to feeling stuck or left out.
About an untested easy life; loosely related to a flat, boring life.
Describes life as struggle until death; restates the question, no answer.
Offers a point: giving life to a high ideal gives it value.
Death everywhere, yet the spirit is immortal; a perspective beyond mortality.
Poses the same question death raises; gives nothing to hold.
Since none escape death, wake up and do good; a response to pointlessness.
Only asks what the goal of life is; restates the person's question.
Life and death follow each other, so no need to complain; a calm view.
This world is a means, not the end; reframes the race toward death.
Struggle still gets us somewhere better; a modest reason to go on.
Answers 'what's the point' directly: we live to discover beauty.
A circle of light remains in every heart; hope amid human darkness.
Be good and merciful to sufferers; don't carry the world's cure alone.
World always mixes good and evil; sympathise and grow stronger through it.
Wars will come; don't be troubled. Steadiness in face of world news.
'If I am evil the world is evil' could imply blame for seeing darkness.
Outer conflict can be borne with inner peace; speaks to keeping darkness out.
Like the sun, the inner Self is not stained by the world's misery.
Don't lose sleep over the world; calm, loving people do real good.
Light shines in darkness and isn't overcome; exactly the needed hope.
Suggests the world mirrors your thoughts; dismisses real war and poverty.
About love of God beyond intellect; not about conversion or the relationship.
Realisation over argument; only loosely touches insincere conversion.
No one need convert; each grows by their own law. Speaks to the core.
My religion cannot be yours; each takes their own road. Directly relevant.
Virtue over outward dress, but urges submitting will to God; mismatched.
Religion is realisation, not assent; supports the worry that converting is hollow.
Unselfishness matters more than religious forms; affirms her as she is.
Different natures need different ways; one way for all is harmful.
Defines religion as realisation; general, doesn't address the dilemma.
Urges faith and obedience to guidance; off for a non-religious person's choice.
Consolation for a friend who has died; wrong situation entirely.
On whom to confide in; could read as faulting her for trusting.
Testing friends through misfortune; tangential to a broken confidence.
Close friend turned against me; restates the betrayal only.
Friendship rests on fidelity; helps her see what was broken.
Secret betrayed by a confidant, with a prayer for protection and integrity.
Breaking confidence forfeits trust; validates her shaken sense of trust.
It was my close friend, not an enemy; restates the pain only.
Revealing secrets destroys friendship; names the gravity of what she felt.
On people misunderstanding each other; not about betrayal of trust.
Daily life is the real temple; religion beyond Sunday attendance.
Forms matter only while they express inner life; speaks to hollow ritual.
Religion isn't going to church but an opened heart; validates the doubt.
People make a church; brief and doesn't address hypocrisy or leaving.
Falsehood is everywhere, not just church; directly weighs whether to leave.
Religion is sincere love, not ceremony; a lens on the meaningless ritual.
Faith on authority isn't faith; abstract, touches it only loosely.
Pure religion is caring for the afflicted; contrasts with congregants' conduct.
No devotion without virtue; speaks to morality missing from worship.
Praying to God as Father yet not treating others as brothers; names hypocrisy.
Forgetting what lies behind and pressing on; answers how to move forward.
Concrete ways to let go of resentment toward someone; fits the anger.
Joseph reconciles with family who wronged him; a model of moving past.
A thin one-line tactic for resentment; little to hold here.
Bear indignation patiently; generic, misses the longing and the past.
Prayer about one's own sins of youth; not about the father's wrongs.
Pardoning a confessed mistake; the father hasn't confessed anything here.
Brief resentment tactic; too slight for years of hurt.
About God healing the speaker's pride; off-topic.
Direct anger at God; sidesteps the father and the past.
A beautiful soul can come from any body; consoling though it says 'ugly'.
Worth shouldn't rest on others' opinions; eases comparison with others.
Stop competing on looks you can't win; return to the good that's yours.
Find beauty in love, not the mirror; short but on point.
Your own thoughts wound you; stop warring with yourself. Speaks to self-hatred.
Look into your soul instead of taking others' word for your worth.
You have something better than your flesh; turns from the body.
Stop staring at your image; look toward what you love.
The body is a cloak; it doesn't decide the worth of who you are.
True beauty is a gentle inner spirit; a gentle reframe.
Instruction to eat in moderation; could feel like a lecture amid self-loathing.
Self-lashing and a habit one can't break; mirrors the spiral, no relief.
Hidden inner wound and self-condemnation; restates rather than helps.
Don't be troubled by frailties; accept being human, long to be undespised.
I shouldn't hurt myself, as I wouldn't hurt others; counters self-loathing.
Cryptic line on sorrow; unlikely to land for this person.
You are more than your body; a gentle turn from body-hatred.
About judging others by one's standard on money; off-topic.
Larger self beyond the hungry mouth; obscure, loosely related.
Vow not to overeat; prescriptive and could deepen shame.
Life is for itself, not a spectacle; worth needs no outside proof.
Don't be diverted by others' blame; follow your own nature.
Real life is in your own skin, not others' opinions; directly on point.
Attend to what you feel, not what others say about you.
Making worth depend on others' views is wretched; frees from judgement.
What I must do concerns me, not what people think; independence in a crowd.
What you think of yourself matters more than others' approval.
Measuring yourself as equal, better or worse breeds conflict; on comparing.
Look at whose approval you seek; then you won't crave it.
You're taking others' word for who you are; look into your own soul.
Find your own way, not your father's or mother's; speaks to the core.
Poetry jolts us out of habit; tangential to choosing a course.
Talent is the call; one direction opens freely. Affirms the pull to writing.
One who tries many paths has a hundred chances; eases practicality fears.
Unused strengths bring lifelong unhappiness, with a fair caution against conceit.
Trust guidance, there is a right place; vague for this decision.
Youthful dreams breed disappointment; discouraging and off the question.
Don't postpone the poet's life to earn first; relevant to the dilemma.
Young dreamers foretell the future; loosely encouraging, not about the choice.
Choose work that uses your own qualities; supports following aptitude.
About bearing a brother's wrong; he is the one who did wrong here.
Calling a child a regret would wound a guilty, estranged parent.
Bearing another's injustice; reversed from his situation.
Confronting someone who wronged you; wrong direction and could mislead.
Bear patiently, the storm will calm; generic for guilt and estrangement.
Assumes one never caused pain; he did, so it doesn't fit.
With a child, will fails and soul connects; shows what went wrong and a way.
Prayer for past wrongs to be met with loving kindness; speaks to guilt.
Stand in the child's place rather than command; a path to repair.
Fathers, don't provoke children; true but reads as a rebuke now.
Don't be elated or resentful; general, misses the hurt from his wife.
Addresses the envier, not the one envied; loosely related.
Advice for the one passed over; not his position.
On avoiding envy oneself; tangential to a spouse's coolness.
Others' promotions torment the stalled; helps him understand his wife's reaction.
Ideal of spouses speaking kindly; generic, offers little now.
Envy as hidden praise; could harden him against his wife.
About envying others' experiences; off-topic.
Envious silence is loud; restates his perception, nothing more.
Contentment when others have power; addresses envier, not him.
